moodys.citation_text: Moody's withdrew Tower Health, PA's Baa2 (negative) rating on 2020-07-09 for lack of sufficient information ('Moody's withdraws rating on Tower Health, PA for lack of sufficient information'). No subsequent Moody's rating action on Tower Health was located through 2022-12-31; the rating was therefore Withdrawn (WR) as of the snapshot date and remained withdrawn through the entire 2023-01-01 to 2025-03-31 window.

sp.citation_text: Philadelphia Inquirer (2023-02-08): 'Standard & Poor's downgraded Tower Health's credit rating by two notches, to "B" from "BB-".' The pre-action rating of BB- is the starting (2022-12-31) rating; outlook was Negative going into the action (S&P 'maintained its negative outlook on Tower' per the same article).

fitch.citation_text: Philadelphia Inquirer (2022-09-20): 'Fitch Ratings slashed Tower Health's credit rating to CCC+, downgrading from B+ to CCC+ ... "Default is a real possibility," according to Fitch's definition of CCC ratings.' Fitch does not assign outlooks to issuers in the CCC category. CCC+ was the standing rating as of 2022-12-31.

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Long-term rating lowered two notches from 'BB-' to 'B'; negative outlook maintained
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Ongoing financial losses and extraordinarily low cash reserves; small financial cushion leaves the system 'highly vulnerable'
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: Standard & Poor's downgraded Tower Health's credit rating by two notches, to 'B' from 'BB-,' citing the nonprofit health system's ongoing financial losses and extraordinarily low cash reserves. The ratings agency maintained its negative outlook on Tower because its small financial cushion leaves the system 'highly vulnerable.'

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Long-term issuer rating lowered one notch from 'CCC+' to 'CCC' (some sources report 'CCC-')
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Continued operating losses in the year that ended June 30 (FY2023 operating loss of $137 million on unaudited results) and extraordinarily low cash reserves relative to long-term debt; ~$1.6 billion of total debt outstanding and 39.3 days' cash on hand
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: Bond Buyer (2023-09-21): 'Fitch lowered Tower's long-term issuer rating one-notch to CCC-minus from CCC after its unaudited financial report for fiscal 2023 showed it incurred operating losses of $137 million on the year.' Corroborating Inquirer (2023-09-20): 'Fitch Ratings downgraded Tower Health's credit rating to CCC,' suggesting prior rating was CCC+ from Sep 2022. Note: there is mild source disagreement between CCC and CCC- as the new rating; the Bond Buyer wording 'one-notch ... from CCC' is internally inconsistent and likely refers to the same Sep-2023 action.

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Long-term rating lowered from 'B' to 'CCC+' (two-notch downgrade); negative outlook
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Significant ongoing operating losses expected to continue in fiscal 2024 and a steep decline in unrestricted reserves to a level S&P views as highly vulnerable
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: Becker's Hospital Review (2023-10-05): 'Tower Health, a three-hospital system in West Reading, PA, has had its long-term rating downgraded twice in a matter of weeks by S&P Global and Fitch.' S&P assigned a 1-in-3 chance of further downgrade given the system's negative outlook. The Becker's article is the headline secondary source; the underlying S&P research item is 'Tower Health, PA Long-Term Rating Lowered To CCC+ From B' (October 2023). Note: The exact action date is reported as October 4, 2023 in WebSearch synthesis of the S&P research bulletin; the full S&P press release is paywalled (HTTP 403 to anonymous fetch on spglobal.com and disclosure.spglobal.com), so the date is corroborated but not directly verified verbatim.

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Long-term rating lowered from 'CCC+' to 'CCC'; negative outlook
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Tower's low financial reserves and concerns that Tower might not have the money for $64.6 million in bonds due to be paid off in February 2025; elevated labor costs and inflation exacerbating an already precarious financial position
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: Philadelphia Inquirer (2024-05-22): 'S&P downgraded Tower Health's credit rating, citing concern about bonds due in February.' New rating CCC from CCC+. 'These efforts have been instrumental in reducing Tower Health's operating losses, but the system has also had to contend with elevated labor costs and inflation, which have exacerbated an already precarious financial position.'

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: CCC rating affirmed on outstanding debt; new exchange bonds not rated
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Fitch concluded the proposed bond exchange did not meet its two-pronged test for a distressed debt exchange because it was not undertaken to avoid bankruptcy; viewed the additional flexibility provided by the bondholder transaction as favorable
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: Bond Buyer: 'Fitch affirmed its CCC rating on the outstanding debt June 5, 2024 ... Fitch did not view the proposed deal as a distressed debt exchange after it failed the rating agency's two-pronged test ... but viewed the additional flexibility provided by the bondholder transaction as favorable.'

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Long-term bond rating lowered from 'CCC' to 'CC'; negative outlook
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Announced debt restructuring viewed as a distressed restructuring: although bondholders receive a par exchange offer, existing lenders will not receive principal and interest payments in line with the originally issued bonds because most new bonds lack amortization until 2039; exchange participants must convert 70% of holdings into deferred-amortization series and 30% into other series
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: S&P Global Ratings (2024-06-13): 'Tower Health, PA Bond Rating Lowered To CC From CCC On Announced Debt Restructuring.' Corroborated by Philadelphia Inquirer (2024-06-20): 'Standard & Poor's has downgraded Tower Health's credit rating for the second time in less than a month, to CC from CCC.' S&P described the deal as a 'distressed restructuring.'

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Debt rating lowered from 'CC' to 'D' (default) following close of distressed exchange
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Settlement of the bond exchange and consent solicitation; S&P had pre-announced it would lower the rating to D upon closing and withdraw the rating 30 days thereafter
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: S&P Global Ratings (2024-09-27): 'Tower Health, PA Debt Rating Lowered To D From CC.' Pre-announcement from Bond Buyer: 'When the deal closes in mid-September, S&P will downgrade Tower Health further to D and then the rating would be withdrawn in 30 days.' The bond-exchange settlement date was 2024-09-19 per Tower Health press release (PR Newswire: 'Tower Health Announces Results of Offer to Exchange and Consent Solicitation'). Note: the spglobal.com URL returns 403 to anonymous WebFetch but is the canonical S&P press-release landing page indexed publicly by WebSearch.

rating_actions_in_window.action_detail: Rating withdrawn (~30 days after assignment of 'D')
rating_actions_in_window.rationale: S&P had pre-announced it would withdraw the rating 30 days after the D action; the post-exchange new-money / exchange bonds were issued without an S&P rating
rating_actions_in_window.citation_text: Bond Buyer: 'When the deal closes in mid-September, S&P will downgrade Tower Health further to D and then the rating would be withdrawn in 30 days.' The withdrawal date is INFERRED (~2024-10-27, 30 days after the 2024-09-27 D action); direct primary-source confirmation of the exact withdrawal date was not located via anonymous fetch.

credit_events_in_window.description: S&P classified Tower Health's announced bond exchange and consent solicitation as a 'distressed restructuring.' Tower offered to exchange ~$1.178 billion of existing bonds for new bonds with deferred amortization (most new bonds lack amortization until 2039), with exchange participants required to convert 70% of holdings into deferred-amortization series and 30% into other series. Tower also issued ~$1.335 billion in new revenue bonds through the Berks County Municipal Authority including ~$157.5 million in new-money bonds. The new bonds carry higher interest rates and bondholders received a claim on Tower's real estate as collateral.
credit_events_in_window.citation_text: Bond Buyer: 'Tower Health plans to issue $1.335 billion of revenue bonds through the Berks County Municipal Authority and exchange $1.178 billion of debt for new bonds ... S&P lowered its rating of Tower Health to CC from CCC on June 13 following the announcement of the debt refinancing plan, viewing the deal as a distressed restructuring.' Tower Health PR Newswire announcement: 'Tower Health Announces Offer to Exchange and Consent Solicitation' (2024-07-31).

credit_events_in_window.description: Settlement date of the bond exchange and consent solicitation. Per S&P's criteria the closing of the distressed exchange was treated as a selective default event, triggering the 2024-09-27 D rating action by S&P. Fitch by contrast did not treat the exchange as a distressed debt exchange under its criteria and affirmed CCC on the legacy debt (2024-06-05).
credit_events_in_window.citation_text: Tower Health press release: 'Tower Health Announces Results of Offer to Exchange and Consent Solicitation,' settlement date 2024-09-19. The settlement formally consummated the distressed restructuring.

moodys.citation_text: Moody's withdrew its rating on Tower Health, PA on 2020-07-09 and no subsequent Moody's rating action on Tower Health was located through 2025-03-31. The rating remained Withdrawn (WR) throughout and at the end of the window.

sp.citation_text: S&P downgraded Tower Health to D on 2024-09-27 following close of the distressed exchange and pre-announced that the rating would be withdrawn ~30 days thereafter (~2024-10-27). As of 2025-03-31, Tower Health is Not Rated (NR) by S&P; the post-restructuring exchange and new-money bonds were issued without an S&P rating. Direct primary-source confirmation of the exact withdrawal date was not located via anonymous fetch (spglobal.com returns 403), but Bond Buyer reports the pre-announced withdrawal plan and no public S&P rating on Tower Health is locatable after October 2024.

fitch.citation_text: Fitch affirmed CCC on Tower Health's outstanding debt on 2024-06-05 and did not classify the bond exchange as a distressed debt exchange. No subsequent Fitch rating action through 2025-03-31 was located. Some intermediate-2023 sources report Fitch's standing rating as CCC- rather than CCC (Bond Buyer 2023-09-21 wording is ambiguous); however the consensus of news coverage (Inquirer, Becker's, Chief Healthcare Executive, Bond Buyer) and Fitch's June 5, 2024 affirmation describe the rating as CCC at end-of-window. Fitch does not assign outlooks in the CCC category.

outcome_class_rationale: Tower Health is a verified DEFAULT in the 2023-2025 window via S&P's 2024-09-27 lowering of the long-term debt rating to 'D' following the close of a distressed bond exchange (settlement 2024-09-19). The path is unambiguously multi-notch deterioration: S&P took Tower from BB- (Dec 2022) -> B (Feb 2023) -> CCC+ (Oct 2023) -> CCC (May 2024) -> CC (Jun 2024) -> D (Sep 2024) -> NR (~Oct 2024), a 7-step / ~10-notch slide ending in default and withdrawal. Fitch ran in parallel: CCC+ (Dec 2022) -> CCC/CCC- (Sep 2023) -> CCC affirmed through bond exchange (Jun 2024). Fitch did not classify the exchange as a distressed debt exchange, but S&P did, and under standard muni-credit backtest conventions an S&P 'D' rating action is a default event. Moody's had withdrawn in 2020 and remained WR throughout the window. The hand-curated label 'MULTI_DOWNGRADE' is therefore UNDER-stated — the correct label is DEFAULT (which strictly dominates MULTI_DOWNGRADE in the outcome hierarchy). The credit event is a distressed exchange / selective default, not a Chapter 11 filing; Tower remained operating post-restructuring.
